title: Derived finite-coefficient comparison on pullbacks and constant complexes
statement:
Let $B$ be a finite commutative ring with the discrete topology and let $f:U\to X$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Use the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every scheme $T$ put $\mathscr B_T=(W\mapsto\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|W|),B))^\#$, the coefficient ring sheaf of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Let $E_T$ be the exact coefficient-realization equivalence from sheaves of $B$-modules on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ to $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathscr B_T)$, normalized by the constant-section identification. Write $N_T=E_T\circ\nu_T^*$ for the comparison of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] in this presentation, and $F_f=E_U\circ f_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}\circ E_X^{-1}$ for the exact identified-coefficient inverse image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Superscript $D$ denotes their functors obtained by termwise localization. Then there are natural isomorphisms
$$ F_f^D\circ N_X^D\ \cong\ N_U^D\circ f_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1,D},\qquad
 N_T^D\bigl(Q\underline{P^\bullet}_{T,\mathrm{et}}\bigr)\ \cong\ E_T^D\bigl(Q\underline{P^\bullet}_{T,\mathrm{proet}}\bigr) $$
for every scheme $T$ and every integer-indexed cochain complex $P^\bullet$ of $B$-modules, with no boundedness or finiteness condition on its terms. Here $Q$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms and underlining means termwise constant sheaf with differential induced by that of $P^\bullet$. The first isomorphism is the canonical etale/pro-etale pullback comparison conjugated by $E$, using the unit to cancel $E_X^{-1}E_X$, and then localized. The second is induced by the constant-sheaf comparison natural in every $B$-linear map; in degree $q$ its term is the comparison for $P^q$, and its chain-map square uses $d^q:P^q\to P^{q+1}$. Both are isomorphisms of whole derived objects, natural in derived inputs and in chain maps, using the recorded coefficient realization and canonical coefficient pullbacks.

proof.text:
Let $u_X:\mathrm{id}\xrightarrow{\sim}E_X^{-1}E_X$ be the unit of the specified coefficient equivalence, and let $c_f:
u_U^*f_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}f_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}
u_X^*$ be [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] for the fixed ring $B$. For an etale $B$-module sheaf $A$ define $b_{f,A}$ by the composite $$E_U f_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}E_X^{-1}E_X
u_X^*A\xrightarrow{E_U f_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}(u_{X,
u_X^*A}^{-1})}E_U f_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}
u_X^*A\xrightarrow{E_U(c_{f,A}^{-1})}E_U
u_U^*f_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}A.$$ Each factor is an isomorphism natural in $A$. Thus $b_f:F_fN_X\xrightarrow{\sim}N_U f_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}$ is precisely the conjugated comparison with unit cancellation specified in the statement. In Lean take exactly the module-functor isomorphism prescribed by the first equality, using comparisonUpperStarCompUpperStarIso and the inverse unit of finiteCoefficientRealization.asEquivalence; reflexivity proves its normalization.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-exact-derived-natural-iso] to $b_f$ between the exact functors $F_fN_X$ and $N_U f_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}$. Using the normalized composition isomorphisms of [lem-sfb-exact-derived-composition] on either side gives $$F_f^D N_X^D\cong(F_fN_X)^D\xrightarrow{D(b_f)}(N_U f_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1})^D\cong N_U^D f_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1,D}.$$ The normalization in those two cited statements identifies its value on every localized complex with the localization of the termwise $b_f$ from step 2, through the factors $a_H$. It is therefore the required canonical first comparison, natural on the whole derived category. The published Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso and Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso implement these normalized localizations directly. Take the composite prescribed by the second equality; its normalization is reflexive, without using a separate uniqueness theorem.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module] to $
u_T$ and every $B$-module $M$. It supplies $k_M:
u_T^*\underline M_{T,\mathrm{et}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline M_{T,\mathrm{proet}}$, natural in every $B$-linear map, with the canonical constant-scalar identification. For the arbitrary complex $P^ ullet$, set $k_P^q=k_{P^q}$. Naturality at $d^q$ gives $$k_{P^{q+1}}\,
u_T^*(\underline {d^q}_{T,\mathrm{et}})=\underline {d^q}_{T,\mathrm{proet}}\,k_{P^q}.$$ Thus the degreewise maps form a chain map; multiplying this equation by the component inverses gives the chain-map equation for $(k_P^q)^{-1}$. They are inverse chain maps, yielding an isomorphism $k_P:C(
u_T^*)\underline {P^ ullet}_{T,\mathrm{et}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline {P^ ullet}_{T,\mathrm{proet}}$. For any chain map $v:P^ ullet	o R^ ullet$, naturality at each $v^q$ gives the chain-level naturality square for $k_P$. In the published fixed-ring sheaf presentation this natural comparison is already constructed as comparisonUpperStarConstantSheafIso, by uniqueness of left adjoints to global sections. Functor.mapHomologicalComplexCompIso gives the complete chain-level natural isomorphism, including its inverse, so no conversion from the general ringed-module lift is necessary.

Put $K=\underline {P^ ullet}_{T,\mathrm{et}}$. By [lem-sfb-exact-derived-composition], [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], and step 4, compose $$N_T^D(QK)\cong E_T^D(
u_T^{*,D}(QK))\xrightarrow{E_T^D(a_{
u_T^*,K})}E_T^D(Q C(
u_T^*)K)\xrightarrow{E_T^D(Q(k_P))}E_T^D(Q\underline {P^ ullet}_{T,\mathrm{proet}}).$$ All arrows are isomorphisms of whole derived objects. The chain-map equations and naturality from step 4 persist under $Q$ and $E_T^D$, and the first two arrows are natural by the cited factorizations. This proves the second comparison and its naturality in chain maps, using exactly the chosen $E_T$. The construction works separately in every integer degree, including zero terms and infinite modules, so imposes no bounds or termwise finiteness. Whisker the composition comparison on the left by the constant-complex functor followed by Q; whisker the comparison localization factor by realization, then whisker the chain comparison by Q and realization. Their composite is gamma as a natural isomorphism of functors. Iso.ext, the component equations for whiskering and functoriality reduce the stated component formula to reflexivity.
